passages.quote:
Introduction

Contact a tribunal office or the customer contact centre if you would like a copy of this publication in an alternative format:

England and Wales: 0300 323 0196

Welsh Speakers: 0300 303 5176

Scotland: 0300 790 6234

Presidential guidance

Under the rules, the presidents of the employment tribunals in England and Wales and Scotland may issue presidential guidance. The aim of that guidance is to improve consistency in the way employment tribunals manage cases and enable the parties to better understand what is expected of them and what to expect.

It is not binding but should be followed where possible.

Go to the presidential guidance in England and Wales and the presidential guidance in Scotland.

Publication of employment tribunal judgments

Judgments issued to parties from February 2017 are published on the online public register.

Under rule 65, a copy of any judgment and any written full reasons for a judgment must be entered into the register.

An employment tribunal has the power, under rule 49 to make an order with a view to preventing or restricting the public disclosure of any aspect of the tribunal proceedings but it can only make such an order if one or more very strict conditions are met. Rule 49 gives more detail about these conditions.

Under rule 49, it is possible for an employment tribunal to make an order which places restrictions on what may be published in the register. This can include, for example, an order which anonymises the name of one or more individuals referred to in the judgment.

Challenge the tribunal’s judgment

Employment tribunal judgments may be changed only:

if the tribunal decides to reconsider the judgment at the request of either party or on its own initiative

after an appeal by one of the parties (see below)

If you disagree with the judgment

If you disagree with the judgment, you may ask the employment tribunal to reconsider the judgment, if reconsideration is necessary in the interests of justice.

You may also appeal to the Employment Appeal Tribunal (EAT) if there is a mistake in the judgment on a point of law. These processes are different, and you will need to decide whether to follow either or both.

You can ask for written reasons for the judgment if the judgment does not have reasons with it. If the tribunal gave summary reasons at the hearing, you can request written summary reasons. After they have been provided you can request written full reasons.

The tribunal may provide full written reasons anyway when you ask for written summary reasons. If the Tribunal gave full reasons at the hearing, you can request written full reasons.

There are strict time limits for asking for written summary reasons and written full reasons, applying for reconsideration and appealing.

Time limits

Ask for written summary reasons

You must apply within 14 days of the date the judgment was sent.

You can only ask for written summary reasons if they were given at the hearing.

Ask for written full reasons

You must apply within:

14 days of the date the judgment was sent, if full reasons were given at the hearing

14 days of the date written summary reasons were sent, if you requested them

Apply for reconsideration

You must apply within 14 days of the latest of the following:

the date the judgment was sent

the date written summary reasons were sent (if you asked for them)

the date written full reasons were sent (if you asked for them, or the tribunal sent them after your request for summary reasons)

Appeal

You must appeal within either:

42 days of the date the reserved judgment with full reasons was sent

42 days of the date separate written full reasons were sent, if you asked for them or the Tribunal sent them after you requested summary reasons

If you do not ask for full reasons and the tribunal does not provide them, you must appeal within 42 days of the date the written record of the judgment was sent.

All appeals must be received by 4pm on the final day.

Further guidance on lodging an appeal can be found in:

How to appeal to the employment appeal tribunal (T440)

Practice direction of the Employment Appeal Tribunal 2024

You can get an appeal form from:

Employment Appeal Tribunal

Fetter Lane

London

EC4A 1NL

Or, in Scotland from:

If you have any questions about the appeal you should address them to the registrar of the EAT. You can also get appeal forms and general information about the EAT.

You must send a copy of any claim and response, the tribunal judgment and the written reasons for the judgment with your notice of appeal or an explanation as to why any missing document is not included. Find out how to ask for written reasons for the judgment.

You must serve a valid notice of appeal on the EAT at:

Employment Appeal Tribunal

7 Rolls Buildings

Fetter Lane

London

EC4A 1NL

Or, in Scotland from:

Employment Appeal Tribunal

George House

126 George Street

Edinburgh

EH2 4HH

If you have not received an acknowledgement from the EAT within 7 days of posting the notice of appeal, you should contact the EAT to confirm they have received your appeal.
